headline: Underwriting holds firm as investment gains cool
summary_short: RenaissanceRe's Q2 2026 net income fell 20.6% y/y to $663.1 million ($15.48 diluted EPS) as investment gains cooled, even as underwriting income held flat at $599.1 million and the combined ratio improved 2.3pts to 72.8%. Book value per share rose 5.7% q/q to $264.77.
summary_long: Underwriting income was roughly flat at $599.1M (combined ratio 72.8%, -2.3pts y/y) as lower catastrophe losses and Bermuda tax credits offset less-favorable prior-year reserve development. Net premiums written fell $493.3M y/y on rate and exposure reductions plus higher Casualty & Specialty retrocession purchases. Total investment result dropped $211.2M as realized/unrealized losses on fixed-income and commodity positions outweighed a $19.4M rise in net investment income. Net income to common fell 20.6% y/y to $663.1M, but $350.0M of Q2 buybacks (part of a renewed $750.0M authorization) helped book value per share rise 5.7% q/q to $264.77. Management's outlook commentary was qualitative only — no numeric forward guidance was issued for revenue, EPS, or premiums.

drivers.explanation: Underwriting income of $599.1M was roughly flat vs Q2 2025 ($601.7M); combined ratio improved 2.3pts to 72.8% on lower catastrophe losses, partly offset by less favorable prior-year development, plus a 1.9pt expense-ratio improvement from Bermuda tax credits.

Gross and net premiums written fell $426.8M and $493.3M y/y, reflecting rate reductions and exposure reductions across both segments plus increased retrocessional coverage purchased in Casualty & Specialty.

Total investment result fell $211.2M y/y, driven by a $228.1M swing to net realized/unrealized losses on fixed-maturity and commodity investments (higher market yields, lower gold futures prices), partly offset by equity-futures gains.
Diluted EPS fell 10.0% y/y, a smaller decline than net income's 20.6% drop, because weighted diluted shares outstanding fell 12.1% y/y (47.3M to 41.5M) from continued buybacks.
Rose 5.7% q/q to $264.77 as retained net income to common outpaced the $350.0M of shares repurchased in the quarter under the renewed $750.0M authorization.
Cash fell y/y as financing outflows (common-share buybacks, DaVinci share repurchases, and distributions to third-party investors in managed joint ventures) exceeded operating cash generation.
